processing: Used for fully oxidised black tea (wakocha): withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented here; Japanese black tea is typically made from spring and summer flushes.
appearance_dry: Dark, twisted leaf, as is typical of Japanese black tea.
appearance_wet: Brown to coppery whole and broken leaf.
taste_profile: Black tea from an Assam-type hybrid typically gives a full, malty cup with noticeable astringency; specific notes vary by maker.

brewing.notes: Western style in a pot; add milk if it is too firm.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's harvest in small lots from individual growers; it is not usually aged. Check the label, since cultivar-named wakocha is made in small amounts and not every year.
description:
Benihomare is a Japanese tea cultivar developed for black tea. It is chiefly known today as the mother plant of Benifuuki, a better-known cultivar, rather than for its own cups.

It is described as an Assam-type hybrid, which in the cup usually means a fuller, stronger and more astringent tea than the usual Japanese green-tea cultivars give.

Because it is rarely sold under its own name, details of its flavour are patchy. Treat the notes here as typical of an Assam-type black tea and trust the maker's description of the actual lot.

If you see it on a label from a small Japanese grower, it is worth trying beside a Benifuuki black tea to taste the family resemblance.
history:
Benihomare was a black tea cultivar of the Assam-hybrid type. It was chosen as the seed parent when Benifuuki was bred, in a cross begun in 1965, with the Darjeeling-type line Makura Cd86 as the pollen parent, because it ferments well and makes good black tea.

Its own breeding date and history are not confirmed here.
